# Implementation Plan: Codex app-server idle-timeout — D-001 defer-and-instrument
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"codex-app-server-idle-timeout"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-07. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan .ralph/jobs/codex-app-server-idle-timeout/plan.md` — but HOLD for operator review first (this is the terminal deliverable of a defer-and-instrument decision).*

## Overview

The codex app-server idle-timeout question ("when the last happy-cli client
disconnects, how long before the process exits?") is resolved by brainstorm
direction **D-001: defer-and-instrument**. Today happy-cli spawns `codex
app-server` as a **detached** ws child that **outlives** the foreground CLI as a
reattachable orphan — effectively "no idle timeout." A happy-cli/TypeScript idle
timer cannot fix this (the **detach-and-exit trap**: the TS timer dies exactly
when happy-cli exits, the moment the orphan is created, so it can never reap the
orphan). The only correct home for an idle timer is the codex process itself
(Rust, deferred as D-002) or a new supervisor (rejected).

This plan therefore ships only the **cheap, reversible scaffolding**, entirely in
**happy-cli (TypeScript)** with **zero codex Rust edits and zero codex-submodule
changes**: (1) an opt-in `--idle-timeout <seconds>` **fresh-spawn-only
spawn-flag seam** that passes the flag to `codex app-server` **only** for a new
ws app-server spawn and **only** when a `codex app-server --help` capability
probe confirms codex advertises it (fail-closed no-op otherwise), default OFF;
(2) real **RSS sampling** wired into the already-stubbed telemetry
path so the sidecar's `rss_kb_at_exit` carries the latest best-effort cached
sample taken at a prior lifecycle event, and the doctor live-row RSS shows a
real-time probe where a platform-reliable source exists; (3) a **last-disconnect
age distribution** surfaced read-only in `happy codex doctor` so the eventual
"sane default" timeout can be informed by the time since the latest observed
client-side disconnect. True server-idle age requires a server-side active-client
signal and stays deferred with D-002/D-003. A manual `happy codex
kill-idle` reaper (D-004) is evaluated and **recommended for deferral** (it is
not "cheap" without a cross-cwd terminator refactor — see Open Questions). The
irreversible auto-exit policy (D-002 server-Rust self-exit, D-003
tunnels-heartbeat) stays **explicitly deferred** until telemetry proves orphans
cost real RSS/ports AND a real multi-device handoff exists to protect.

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context

Seeded from brainstorm: `.ralph/brainstorms/codex-app-server-idle-timeout/selected-direction.md` (D-001, operator-selected). Full research brief: `.ralph/jobs/codex-app-server-idle-timeout/research-brief.md`. All four lenses (researcher, architect, codex-exec xhigh, copilot-exec xhigh) converged on the same seam design.

- **Reattach-before-spawn behavior:** `connect()` attempts discovery reattach before any ws spawn (`codexAppServerClient.ts:1173-1175`), and `CodexDiscoveryRecord` (`codexAppServerDiscovery.ts:22-33`) does not carry idle-timeout intent. Therefore `--idle-timeout` can only affect a freshly spawned ws app-server in this slice; it must never re-apply or override timeout policy on an already-running daemon.
- **Spawn site (ws):** `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/codexAppServerClient.ts:1185`
  builds the ws argv `['app-server','--listen',listenUrl,'--ws-auth','capability-token','--ws-token-sha256',<sha>]`; `extraAppServerArgs` is appended immediately after at `:1186-1188`. The detached spawn itself is `createWsConnection()` at `:851-888` (`crossSpawn(... detached:true, stdio:['ignore',logFd,logFd] ...)`, `unref()`-ed).
- **Capability-probe precedent:** `isWsAuthAvailable()` (`:148-160`) runs `codex app-server --help` and checks `helpOutput.includes('--ws-auth')`; `getWsAuthAvailability()` (`:947-951`) memoizes it in `wsAuthProbeResult` (`:272`) per `CodexAppServerClient` instance; the fallback/fail-closed logic is at `:291-301` and `:1092-1104`.
- **Opt-in threading precedent:** structured flags are parsed by `extract*Flag()` helpers in `cliArgs.ts` (e.g. `extractCodexArgFlag` `:259-292`), chained in `codexCommand.ts:23-30`, passed to `runCodex(...)` `:41-52`, which constructs `new CodexAppServerClient(sandboxConfig, { transport, transportSource, logFilePath, extraAppServerArgs })` at `runCodex.ts:701-706`. The client stores `extraAppServerArgs` (`:288`) via `CodexAppServerClientOptions` (`:91-103`).
- **Telemetry sidecar (already ~95% wired):** `codexDaemonLifecycle.ts:29-55` is a `.strict()` snake_case discriminated union; the `codex.daemon.exit` event **already** carries `uptime_ms`, `rss_kb_at_exit`, and `last_client_disconnect_age_ms`, and `codex.daemon.disconnect` carries `last_client_disconnect_age_ms`. The exit emitter already writes `rss_kb_at_exit: this.lastSampledRssKb` (`codexAppServerClient.ts:772`) and `uptime_ms` (`:771`). The RSS sampler `refreshLastSampledRssKb(_pid)` (`:728-730`) is a **no-op stub that always sets `null`**, and is already invoked at spawn (`:1298`), reattach (`:1030`), disconnect (`:1386`), and synthetic-exit (`:750`, gated by `opts.refreshRss`).
- **Doctor:** `codexDaemonDoctor.ts` renders a read-only table (columns `state,pid,endpoint,cwd,age,RSS,last-health,last-disconnect,exit_reason,version`, `:154-177`), with `probeCodexDaemon()` (`:180-247`, RSS currently null), `classifyCodexDaemonState()` (`:249-259`), and `runCodexDoctor()` summary + exit-code matrix (`:268-335`). Dispatched before auth/daemon-startup at `codexCommand.ts:16-20`. A `last-disconnect` cell already exists (`:145-148`, `humanizeDuration`).
- **RSS dependency:** `ps-list` is already a dependency (`package.json:68-120`), but its `memory` field is `%mem`, not RSS-KB, and is unsupported on Windows (`docs/codex-daemon-lifecycle.md:205-208`).
- **Env/config:** `configuration.ts:32-79` (HAPPY_* reads), `utils/envNames.ts:1-4` (env-name constants) — where an optional `HAPPY_CODEX_IDLE_TIMEOUT` would slot if env opt-in is later added.
- **Tests:** command is `pnpm run build && vitest run` (`package.json:60-66`); on Windows/Git Bash use `npm_config_script_shell=bash pnpm --filter happy test` or `pnpm --filter happy exec vitest run <paths>` for file-scoped runs. Patterns: `codexAppServerClient.test.ts` mocks `execSync` for the help probe and spies on `./codexDaemonTelemetry`; `codexDaemonDoctor.test.ts` asserts RSS-null + exit-code + post-mortem; `cliArgs.test.ts` / `codexCommand.test.ts` cover flag extraction.

### Technical Constraints

- **Detached ws orphan is load-bearing** — do NOT add any TS-side timer; the seam only passes a flag the codex process itself would honor.
- **Zero codex / Rust / submodule footprint.** Upstream app-server has no process-level idle-exit flag (only thread-level 30-min unload), so the flag the seam targets does not exist in codex yet → the probe MUST fail closed.
- **`.strict()` snake_case append-only sidecar** — fields may be populated but not renamed; additions must extend the discriminated union (avoid unless required; here no schema change is needed).
- **Security:** the raw ws capability token must never reach argv/env/logs/sidecar (only the sha256 is persisted). The idle-timeout flag and value are non-secret.
- **WS-only seam.** stdio is foreground-owned (no detached orphan), so idle-timeout is injected only in the ws spawn branch, never stdio or sandbox-wrapped stdio. Sandbox forces stdio on non-Windows (`:1086-1090`).
- **Doctor stays strictly read-only** — no rotate/prune/kill/restart/delete; exit-code matrix preserved.
- **RSS must not misreport `%mem` as RSS-KB** — use a real platform-aware source or return `null`.

## Approach

### Architecture

Three independently-valuable, file-overlapping changes plus docs:

1. **Spawn-flag seam + capability probe** — mirror the ws-auth machinery exactly. Add a single source-of-truth flag constant `CODEX_IDLE_TIMEOUT_FLAG = '--idle-timeout'`; add `isIdleTimeoutAvailable()` (runs `codex app-server --help`, checks `includes(CODEX_IDLE_TIMEOUT_FLAG)`) and an instance-cached `getIdleTimeoutAvailability()` (new `idleTimeoutProbeResult: boolean | null` field). Thread an opt-in integer-seconds value `happy codex --idle-timeout <seconds>` through `codexCommand.ts` → `extractCodexIdleTimeoutFlag()` → `runCodex.ts` → a new `idleTimeoutSec?: number` option on `CodexAppServerClientOptions`. In `codexCommand.ts`, keep `extractCodexArgFlag()`'s value-consumption authoritative by running it before `extractCodexIdleTimeoutFlag()` (after the existing transport extraction), then parse idle-timeout from `codexArgs.args`; this ensures `happy codex --codex-arg --idle-timeout=30` is passed through verbatim instead of being consumed as the structured flag. In the **ws** spawn loop only, when `idleTimeoutSec != null` **and** `getIdleTimeoutAvailability()` is true, append `[CODEX_IDLE_TIMEOUT_FLAG, String(idleTimeoutSec)]` to the ws argv **before** `extraAppServerArgs` (so a power-user `--codex-arg` still wins). This is explicitly **fresh-spawn-only**: `tryReattach()` runs before this spawn loop and the discovery record has no timeout field, so an invocation with `--idle-timeout` must attach to an existing daemon without re-applying, overriding, or validating that daemon's timeout policy. When unsupported: emit nothing to argv and log exactly one non-error line (guarded by a `idleTimeoutFallbackWarned` flag, mirroring `wsAuthFallbackWarned`). Default `undefined` ⇒ OFF ⇒ argv unchanged.
   - **Recommended refinement (Story 1):** since both `isWsAuthAvailable()` and the new probe shell out to the identical `codex app-server --help`, consolidate to a single cached `getAppServerHelpText()` read that both capability checks consume, so connect() shells out to `--help` at most once. (Optional; see OQ-1.)
2. **RSS sampling** — implement a new `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/processRss.ts` exporting `sampleProcessRssKb(pid: number): Promise<number | null>` with a **pinned platform matrix** so two implementers cannot diverge: **Linux** reads `/proc/<pid>/statm` (RSS pages × page size → KB) or falls back to `ps -o rss= -p <pid>` (KB); **macOS** uses `ps -o rss= -p <pid>` (KB); **Windows** returns `null` for v1 (no reliable true-RSS-KB source without extra tooling — see OQ-3); a dead/stale/unknown pid returns `null` and never throws. Replace the body of `refreshLastSampledRssKb()` (`:728-730`) to call it (keeping all four existing call sites). Preserve the existing observable-exit behavior: `emitObservableExitEvent()` does **not** re-sample at child exit because the pid may already be gone, so `rss_kb_at_exit` is the latest cached sample from spawn/reattach/disconnect (or synthetic-exit refresh when Happy initiates termination), not a guaranteed exit-time reading. Also call the sampler from `probeCodexDaemon()` so live doctor rows show real-time RSS. No sidecar-schema change (`rss_kb_at_exit` already exists).
3. **Doctor last-disconnect age distribution** — reuse/extend the existing `last-disconnect` cell with a derived per-instance **last-disconnect age** value (live/stale: `now - latest observed client-side disconnect`; post-mortem: the exit event's `last_client_disconnect_age_ms`), plus a compact **bucket summary** (`<1h` / `1-24h` / `>24h` / `unknown`) appended to `runCodexDoctor()`'s summary line. This is not true server-idle age; true idle-age requires a server-side active-client count and stays deferred with D-002/D-003. Read-only; no schema change.
4. **Docs** — update `packages/happy-cli/docs/codex-daemon-lifecycle.md` for the fresh-spawn-only seam + probe semantics, real RSS sampling, and the doctor last-disconnect age surfacing.

`happy codex kill-idle` (D-004) is **scoped as optional and recommended for deferral**: the existing terminators (`terminateAttachedAppServer` / `closeWsChild`, `:803-849`) are private and delete only the **current-cwd** `discoveryFilePath()`, so a cross-cwd reaper needs a shared per-discovery-file terminator + lock refactor — that fails the seed's "IF cheap" gate (2 of 3 external lenses agree). See OQ-5 for the minimal-standalone-reaper alternative if the operator wants it in-slice.

### Implementation Strategy

Order is dictated by file overlap (two central files are shared):

1. **US-001 seam+probe** first (touches `codexAppServerClient.ts` + cliArgs/command/runCodex).
2. **US-002 RSS** second (also touches `codexAppServerClient.ts`, plus new `processRss.ts` and `codexDaemonDoctor.ts`).
3. **US-003 doctor last-disconnect age** third (also touches `codexDaemonDoctor.ts`).
4. **US-005 docs** last (reflects 1–3).
5. **US-004 kill-idle** only if the operator opts in (depends on 1–3).

Because US-001/US-002 share `codexAppServerClient.ts` and US-002/US-003 share `codexDaemonDoctor.ts`, **serial single-member execution is recommended** (see Suggested Decomposition).

## Scope

### In Scope
- Opt-in `happy codex --idle-timeout <seconds>` ws-spawn-flag seam, gated by a fail-closed `codex app-server --help` capability probe, default OFF.
- Fresh-spawn-only timeout semantics: reattach to an existing discovery record never re-applies, overrides, or checks the requested idle-timeout value.
- Single source-of-truth flag constant shared by probe + argv emission.
- Per-instance probe caching mirroring ws-auth.
- Real RSS sampler (`processRss.ts`) wired into the existing `refreshLastSampledRssKb()` stub and `probeCodexDaemon()`; `null` on platforms without a reliable true-RSS source.
- Read-only `happy codex doctor` last-disconnect age per-instance value + bucket-summary distribution.
- Docs + tests (extend existing suites + new sampler test).
- `happy codex kill-idle` **only if** the operator accepts the cross-cwd-terminator refactor (otherwise deferred).

### Out of Scope
- **ANY** edit to `codex/` (Rust) or the codex submodule pointer. Zero.
- D-002 (server-owned Rust idle-exit), including the server-side active-client count required for true idle-age, and D-003 (tunnels heartbeat-driven exit) — explicitly deferred.
- Building a TS-side idle timer of any kind.
- Choosing/enabling a default idle-timeout value (chosen later, from the data this slice produces).
- Env/config opt-in surface (`HAPPY_CODEX_IDLE_TIMEOUT`) — deferred to a follow-up unless trivially free during US-001.
- Discovery-record timeout intent field plus reattach compatibility enforcement — deferred follow-up; this slice keeps the v1 discovery schema unchanged.
- Applying idle-timeout to stdio/sandbox-wrapped-stdio spawns.
- `app-server-daemon` crate / remote-control paths.

## Risk Areas

- **Flag-spelling uncertainty.** codex does not expose `--idle-timeout` today; the seam must fail closed and the detection string must be one constant so a later spelling/unit change is a single edit. Mitigation: `CODEX_IDLE_TIMEOUT_FLAG` constant + probe `.includes()` it; AC-2 asserts no-op when absent.
- **Double `--help` shell-out.** Adding a second probe could shell out to `codex app-server --help` twice per connect. Mitigation: optional shared cached help read (OQ-1).
- **Reattach hides timeout intent.** Because reattach is attempted before spawn and the v1 discovery record has no timeout field, `--idle-timeout 60` may attach to a no-timeout daemon, and a later default-OFF invocation may attach to a timeout-enabled daemon after codex grows the flag. Mitigation: document the seam as fresh-spawn-only and add a regression test that reattach does not re-apply or override timeout policy; defer discovery timeout metadata + compatibility checks.
- **Windows RSS source.** `ps-list.memory` is `%mem`, unsupported as RSS on Windows. Mitigation: `processRss.ts` returns `null` on unsupported platforms; never coerce `%mem`. AC-5 scopes this explicitly.
- **Doctor read-only invariant.** New last-disconnect-age/RSS rendering must not mutate state or change exit codes. Mitigation: render-only changes + existing doctor read-only tests.
- **Test-harness boundaries.** Keep telemetry I/O behind the `codexDaemonTelemetry` spy; mock `execSync` for the probe; assert spawn argv in the existing client harness.
- **kill-idle scope creep.** A naive cross-cwd reaper would need to refactor private current-cwd terminators. Mitigation: default-defer; document the minimal standalone-reaper alternative (OQ-5).
- **Zero-codex-footprint regression.** Final diff must be `packages/happy-cli/**` only. Mitigation: AC-8 path-list check.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC-1 (seam passes flag only when supported):** With `--idle-timeout <n>` set AND the help probe reporting the flag, the captured ws spawn argv contains `--idle-timeout <n>` (asserted in the mocked client harness).
- **AC-1a (passthrough parser ordering preserved):** `happy codex --codex-arg --idle-timeout=30` is parsed as a passthrough codex arg and forwarded verbatim in `codexAppServerArgs`, while bare `happy codex --idle-timeout 30` is parsed structurally into `codexIdleTimeoutSec` and not forwarded as a passthrough arg (assert in `cliArgs.test.ts` and/or `codexCommand.test.ts`).
- **AC-1b (flag validation):** `extractCodexIdleTimeoutFlag()` accepts only a positive integer number of seconds and rejects — each with a clear, specific error — zero, negative, non-integer/non-numeric, empty `--idle-timeout=`, missing value (`--idle-timeout` at end of argv), and duplicate occurrences; every rejection case is covered in `cliArgs.test.ts`.
- **AC-2 (fail-closed no-op):** With the help probe NOT reporting the flag, ws argv contains no idle-timeout token, the client still connects (reattach-forever unchanged), and at most one non-error log line is emitted (verified via `execSync` help-mock without the flag).
- **AC-3 (default OFF):** With no `--idle-timeout` opt-in, no idle-timeout token is ever added regardless of probe result; spawn argv is byte-for-byte unchanged vs today.
- **AC-3a (reattach does not apply timeout):** When a valid discovery record already exists and `tryReattach()` succeeds, a `happy codex --idle-timeout <n>` invocation reattaches without spawning, does not call the idle-timeout capability probe for argv construction, and does not attempt to re-apply, override, or reject the existing daemon based on timeout policy (asserted in the client reattach test harness).
- **AC-4 (probe cached per instance):** The idle-timeout `codex app-server --help` probe runs at most once per `CodexAppServerClient` instance (assert mocked help-call count across multiple connect attempts), matching ws-auth caching. If OQ-1's shared-help refinement is taken, assert `--help` is invoked at most once total per instance.
- **AC-5 (RSS populated where feasible):** On a platform with a reliable RSS source, `rss_kb_at_exit` carries the latest best-effort cached KB sample taken at the most recent lifecycle sampling point before exit (spawn/reattach/disconnect, or synthetic-exit refresh when Happy initiates termination), and the doctor live-row RSS is populated from a real-time `probeCodexDaemon()` sample; on unsupported platforms (Windows for v1) both stay `null` and `%mem` is never reported as RSS-KB. `sampleProcessRssKb` returns `null` (never throws) for a dead/stale/unknown pid. Coverage: `processRss.test.ts` exercises Linux (`/proc`/`ps -o rss=`), macOS (`ps -o rss=`), Windows-null, and dead-pid → null; telemetry-module + doctor-render tests cover the cached-exit vs live-probe split.
- **AC-6 (last-disconnect age surfaced in doctor):** `happy codex doctor` reuses/extends the existing `last-disconnect` cell to render a per-instance last-disconnect age (live/stale: now - latest observed client-side disconnect; post-mortem: exit `last_client_disconnect_age_ms`) AND a bucket-summary distribution (`<1h`/`1-24h`/`>24h`/`unknown`) across live + post-mortem instances; it must not label this value as true idle-age, because true server-idle age requires a deferred server-side active-client count; doctor remains read-only with the exit-code matrix intact.
- **AC-7 (kill-idle — DEFAULT: deferred):** The v1 default is **deferred** (see OQ-5: cross-cwd reaping is not "cheap" without a terminator refactor). IF the operator opts in during review, `happy codex kill-idle` terminates only operator-selected idle/orphan instance(s), honors the confirm-dead-before-delete + per-cwd-lock invariants, and is a clear no-op when nothing is idle. When deferred (the default), this AC does not apply.
- **AC-8 (zero codex/Rust footprint):** Final diff touches only `packages/happy-cli/**`; no file under `codex/` changes and no submodule pointer moves (verified by inspecting the diff path list).
- **AC-9 (docs updated):** `packages/happy-cli/docs/codex-daemon-lifecycle.md` documents the telemetry/RSS, the fresh-spawn-only `--idle-timeout` seam + fail-closed probe, the doctor last-disconnect age surface, and why true server-idle age is deferred until a server-side active-client count exists.
- **AC-10 (typecheck + tests green):** `pnpm --filter happy typecheck` (cross-package typecheck) passes and the happy-cli vitest suite is green via `pnpm --filter happy test` (or `pnpm --filter happy exec vitest run <paths>` for file-scoped runs; on Windows/Git Bash prefix `npm_config_script_shell=bash`), including the new seam/RSS/doctor tests.

## Preliminary Story Decomposition

- **US-001 — `--idle-timeout` spawn-flag seam + capability probe.** Flag constant, `isIdleTimeoutAvailable()`/`getIdleTimeoutAvailability()`, `extractCodexIdleTimeoutFlag()`, command+runCodex threading with `extractCodexArgFlag()` consumed before the idle-timeout extractor, ws-only fresh-spawn argv injection, fail-closed no-op + one-time log, passthrough parser-order regression coverage, and reattach regression coverage proving the flag is not re-applied to an existing daemon. (AC-1,1a,2,3,3a,4,8) — medium.
- **US-002 — Real RSS sampling.** `processRss.ts` + wire into `refreshLastSampledRssKb()` and `probeCodexDaemon()`; exit telemetry uses the last cached lifecycle sample, live doctor rows use a real-time probe sample, and unsupported platforms return null. (AC-5,8) — medium.
- **US-003 — Doctor last-disconnect age distribution.** Per-instance last-disconnect age + bucket summary, read-only, reusing/extending the existing `last-disconnect` cell. (AC-6,8) — small/medium.
- **US-004 — (Optional) `happy codex kill-idle`.** Default-deferred; include only with the cross-cwd terminator refactor. (AC-7) — medium/large.
- **US-005 — Docs.** Update the lifecycle contract doc. (AC-9) — small.

## Suggested Decomposition

Two central files are shared across stories (`codexAppServerClient.ts` by US-001+US-002; `codexDaemonDoctor.ts` by US-002+US-003), so **serial single-member execution is recommended**. Clusters below form a serial chain.

### Cluster: seam-and-probe
- Stories: US-001
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`codexAppServerClient.ts`]; exclusive=[`cliArgs.ts`, `commands/codexCommand.ts`, `runCodex.ts`]; risk=medium
- `execution_mode` rationale: Must land first; it introduces the flag constant + probe + `idleTimeoutSec` option that later edits to `codexAppServerClient.ts` build on. Serialize because it shares the central client file with the RSS cluster.

### Cluster: rss-sampling
- Stories: US-002
- Phase: 2
- Depends on: seam-and-probe
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`codexAppServerClient.ts`, `codexDaemonDoctor.ts`]; exclusive=[`processRss.ts`]; risk=medium
- `execution_mode` rationale: Edits `refreshLastSampledRssKb()` in the same client file as US-001 and touches the doctor probe shared with US-003 — must serialize after seam-and-probe and before doctor-last-disconnect-age to avoid conflicting edits on both shared files.

### Cluster: doctor-last-disconnect-age
- Stories: US-003
- Phase: 3
- Depends on: rss-sampling
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`codexDaemonDoctor.ts`]; exclusive=[]; risk=medium
- `execution_mode` rationale: Adds last-disconnect age rendering to the same doctor file the RSS cluster modifies; serialize after rss-sampling.

### Cluster: docs
- Stories: US-005
- Phase: 4
- Depends on: seam-and-probe, rss-sampling, doctor-last-disconnect-age
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[]; exclusive=[`docs/codex-daemon-lifecycle.md`]; risk=low
- `execution_mode` rationale: Documents the shipped behavior; depends on all code clusters. (Optional US-004 kill-idle, if the operator opts in, inserts as phase 3.5 depending on phases 1–3.)

## Open Questions

The acceptance set above is **deterministic**: the AC-affecting questions (OQ-3 RSS platforms, OQ-4 doctor shape, OQ-5 kill-idle) already have v1 defaults baked into AC-5/AC-6/AC-7, so `/implement-with-ralph` can proceed without ambiguity. These remain listed only so the operator can override a default during the HOLD review; OQ-1/OQ-2/OQ-6 are design notes that do not gate any AC.

1. **OQ-1 — Shared `--help` read?** Should US-001 consolidate the ws-auth and idle-timeout probes onto a single cached `getAppServerHelpText()` so connect() shells out to `codex app-server --help` at most once? (Recommended; low risk. AC-4 covers either choice.)
2. **OQ-2 — Opt-in surface.** Ship only the `happy codex --idle-timeout <seconds>` CLI flag now, or also add the `HAPPY_CODEX_IDLE_TIMEOUT` env var in the same slice? (Recommended: CLI flag only now; env deferred unless free.) Confirm units = integer **seconds**.
3. **OQ-3 — Windows RSS source.** **Default chosen for v1 (operator-confirm):** `null` on Windows, populate on macOS/Linux. Is a reliable true-RSS-KB source worth adding on Windows (e.g. WMI/`Get-Process`/tasklist) instead, or does RSS stay `null` on Windows (the fork's dev box)? (Revisit only if the orphan-cost question needs Windows RSS.)
4. **OQ-4 — Doctor last-disconnect age shape.** **Default chosen (operator-confirm):** extend the existing `last-disconnect` cell AND add summary buckets `<1h`/`1-24h`/`>24h`/`unknown`. (Operator may opt for summary-only or different bucket edges.)
5. **OQ-5 — kill-idle include or defer.** **Default chosen (operator-confirm): DEFER** (cross-cwd reaping needs a shared per-discovery-file terminator + lock refactor; not "cheap"). Alternative if the operator wants it in-slice: a minimal standalone reaper (sibling of `codexDaemonDoctor.ts`) that, for a selected discovery record, does its own confirm-dead-before-delete by PID (`isPidAlive` + `process.kill` + recheck) without reusing the private client terminators. Decide include vs defer.
6. **OQ-6 — Telemetry sufficiency.** `last_client_disconnect_age_ms` + `uptime_ms` + RSS suffice to choose a later default for the single-device world, but the device-handoff window cannot be measured until multi-device ships. The plan should state this limit explicitly so the "choose default from data" expectation is calibrated.

*(This plan is on HOLD for operator review before any `/implement-with-ralph` handoff — D-001 is a defer-and-instrument decision and the plan is the terminal deliverable.)*
